content.text:
**Finding submitted — deviation (high severity).**

The agreement's assignment provision (Section 20(d), paragraph p0142) is a flat mutual consent requirement with no affiliate or M&A carve-out for Sparkling and no reasonableness standard — squarely in our walk-away zone. Section 3(c) reinforces the bar by prohibiting Sparkling from assigning "except as and when authorized to do so by Garman in writing." Notably, the agreement contains no change-of-control language at all, so nothing currently confirms that our reorganization or sale won't be treated as a deemed assignment.

Redline validated (ok:true) and filed:
- **p0142** rewritten: Sparkling may assign without consent to an affiliate or to a successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of substantially all assets; Garman may assign only with our prior written consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a competitor; a change of control of Sparkling is not an assignment and gives Garman no termination, suspension or re-pricing right.
- **p0033** conformed with an "except as permitted by Section 20(d)" lead-in so the use restrictions don't override the carve-out.

Fallback offered in the comment: mutual right to assign to successors on written notice, with consent for other assignments not unreasonably withheld.
